  "text": "The boy turned toward the voice. One foot nudged a plate off the table. Mara remembered the breaking sound, though she had always placed it earlier, before the water reached the house.

“Who was I talking to?” she asked.

The ferryman lowered his eyes.

In the mirror, her father appeared in the doorway carrying a length of rope. He was younger than she was now. That seemed indecent: to have outlived his face.

He threw the rope toward Elias. It fell short.

“Again,” Mara whispered.

But her younger self caught her father’s sleeve.

Outside, something struck the wall with a force that shook the plates. Her father stumbled. The girl pulled him toward the door.

Mara remembered his weight against her, his wet shirt clutched in both fists. She had told herself he was pulling her out.

“The rope,” she said. “I could have thrown it.”

“Yes,” said the ferryman.

“Would it have reached?”

“I don’t know.”

She hated him for that more than she would have hated certainty.

Beneath the boat, Elias crouched on the table. Water lifted the fallen plate and carried it past his feet, unbroken.

Mara reached toward him.

The ferryman caught her wrist.

“You can watch until you remember. You cannot stay until it changes.”

On the bank, the grown man waited, wearing the face she had invented for her brother over twenty years.

The boy in the glass was looking at the doorway.

Mara knelt in the warm water.

“Elias,” she said, and this time addressed the child. “I went outside with Father. I didn’t come back.”"
